thread:
anna_ops: FYI rolling update to CUDA 12 toolkit finished in us-west-2 but we're seeing sporadic container failures and a bunch of PTX cache eviction warnings in node logs.

javier: hmm. can you paste the logs? which image revision?

anna_ops: image=redwood/runtime:2026-03-17-cu12
logs:
```
[WARN] ptx cache eviction for module 'sm_86' (size=42MB)
ERROR: failed to load kernel object: -22
[ERR] invalid ELF header while loading ptx blob
```

infra-oncall: noticed a spike in pod restart counts and tail latency on gpu pools, autoscaler spun up new nodes but many failed kubelet healthchecks. rolling-failure pattern.

kai: could be host driver vs toolkit mismatch + compiler/runtime ABI mismatch. host driver on those nodes is 525.89, toolkit is cu12. also we rebuilt containers with gcc13 which can change libstdc++/GLIBCXX symbols. what's the kernel version on the affected hosts?

mira: hosts are 5.10.162, kubelet 1.27. we did a rebuild of all runtime images with GCC13 last night to enable some perf flags. can reproduce locally when I run the container on a cu12 host: PTX compile succeeds but then loader errors.

ops-liz: rollback to cu11 images is an option but that'll force model restarts and cause capacity churn. prefer targeted rollback on the affected pool only (gpuprod-usw2-a). need cost and blast-radius notes.

javier: short-term workaround attempt: can we disable PTX persistence or change the cache dir? runtime has flags: `--ptx-persist=0` and `--ptx-cache-dir=/tmp/ptx` — might reduce eviction storms while we triage.

anna_ops: tried disabling persist on one node; logs show fewer eviction warnings but containers still fail with `invalid ELF header` for a handful of modules. suspect builder produced a different object layout.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0458 - "cu12 runtime regressions in us-west-2" - assigned to eng-infra.

kai: suggested action plan:
1) cordon+drain affected nodes in gpuprod-usw2-a pool (min disruption)
2) pin that pool to cu11 image until we have a validated cu12 artifact
3) run a kernel-module rebuild job to recompile nvidia modules against host GCC to avoid symbol mismatch
4) add extra healthcheck/trace on PTX loader path and increase logging for `libcudart` load failures

mira: starting node drain for pool=gpuprod-usw2-a (drain 1/8). will post progress updates.

ops-liz: please also add a cost estimate to the incident: expect 3-4h of manual ops + potential 10-15% spike in on-demand GPU usage while capacity stabilizes. tagging billing for heads-up.

javier: also filing a bug against the toolkit builder: my hypothesis is the container build pipeline used `-fno-plt` and LTO flags that reorder .ptx sections leading to loader incompatibility. need bisect of build flags vs image hash.

anna_ops: copying logs and a failing image tar to the incident. tagging @security for KMS access if we need to pull private artifacts.

mira: node drain 1/8 complete. running kernel-module rebuild job on drained node now. will validate by restarting a small canary job. :thumbsup:

anna_ops: thanks all — will keep INC-2026-0458 updated with timeline and rollback decisions.
